The Free Levels That reml() Integrates Beside the Coefficients

Source: R/outer.R
free_level_equations.Rd

Returns the equations whose structural level is free and is integrated by reml() as one more column of that equation's design, or character(0) where nothing is added.

Usage

free_level_equations(spec, design, method = NULL, basis = NULL)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

design

The design.

method

An OuterMethod(), or NULL to skip the check of its kind.

basis

The integrated subspace, NULL under reml().

Value

A character vector of distribution parameters, one per free level.

Details

A score-driven level, the first level of modelterms7::regime() and each level of a joint filter add a constant to their equation's predictor. Where an intercept is present the level is held (statmod_held_levels()) and the intercept is integrated as an unpenalized coefficient. Where the level is free, it plays the intercept's part, and the criterion integrates it in the same way: as the constant that it adds to the predictor, a column of ones in its equation. For modelterms7::gas() that constant is the stationary level \(\omega / (1 - \sum_j \xi_j)\), so y ~ x + random(~ 1 | g) + gas() and y ~ 0 + x + random(~ 1 | g) + gas() give the same criterion at every hyperparameter.

The rule applies to reml() on the route over the coefficients, where no penalty covers the term's own parameters; where one does, statmod_marginal_full() already integrates every free parameter of the term. ml() integrates the penalized directions only and is unchanged. A developed level contributes its constant coordinate, the one that modelterms7::term_level_param() names. A model carrying a Jeffreys penalty is left on its own route, whose curvature is factored in two parts.

See also

level_augmented(), statmod_marginal()
